question: Can landlord legally raise rent on one unit but not the other?
short_answer: Yes — if neutral anniversary/bank reason documented; selective increase not per se illegal
legal_standard_detailed: SF Rent Ordinance allows per-unit anniversary timing; Fair Housing Act bars different terms based on protected class not per-unit timing alone. Disparate treatment requires intent or facial neutral policy with disparate impact (Texas v Inclusive Communities).
application_to_unit1_vs_unit2: Unit 1 anniversary Feb 1 Unit 2 June 1 Different eligibility dates = neutral basis. Unit 1 has 1.4% banked $119.85 potential Unit 2 has longer bank potential → different dollar amount but same methodology is neutral. Raising Unit 1 1.6% ($63.92) and leaving Unit 2 at $3150 until June 1 anniversary is lawful.
practical_recommendation: Adopt written policy One increase per unit per 12 mo at Board rate on anniversary plus documented bank — apply to both on own dates — and note reason in file.

question: Does raising only one unit invite discrimination lawsuit?
short_answer: It invites scrutiny but not automatic liability; risk proportional to lack of neutral documentation and correlation with protected class.
legal_standard_detailed: Plaintiff must show statistical disparity caused by policy + lack of business justification (HUD 2023 discriminatory effects burden-shifting). In SF tenant counsel will test selective increase for pretext.
application_to_unit1_vs_unit2: If Unit 2 houses family with children (familial status protected) and Unit 1 does not and you raise only Unit 2 higher → higher inquiry risk even without intent disparate impact review. If both units get same 1.6% methodology risk low.
practical_recommendation: Better to raise both consistently on methodology not ad hoc — safest in tenant-friendly jurisdiction.

question: Would raising both equally avoid discrimination inquiry entirely?
short_answer: It materially lowers risk but does not immunize from other claims (retaliation just cause license)
legal_standard_detailed: Uniform 1.6% on each anniversary shows good faith normal business practice; still must be licensed notice-correct and non-retaliatory.
application_to_unit1_vs_unit2: Both at 1.6% on respective anniversaries Unit 1 $63.92 Unit 2 $50.40 same percentage different dollars — documented as annual allowable — strongest tenant-lawyer proof.
practical_recommendation: Raise both at same lawful percentage on respective anniversaries; 30-day written notice with bank breakdown.

question: What neutral reasons count for different amounts on different units?
short_answer: Different base rents different banked years different anniversary dates — all neutral; occupant behavior or protected trait not neutral.
legal_standard_detailed: $3995×3.0%=$119.85 vs $3150×4.7%=$148.05 different dollars but both reflect neutral bank math — lawful. "Tenant complained" or "tenant has children" not neutral.
application_to_unit1_vs_unit2: Document bank math: Unit 1: banked 1.4% +1.6% =3.0% Unit 2: banked 1.7+1.4+1.6=4.7% — retain calculation sheet.
practical_recommendation: Document additive not compound show years amounts licenses.

question: How to prove non-discrimination in SF tenant-lawyer review?
short_answer: Show (1) consistent written policy (2) anniversary alignment (3) license (4) 30/90 compliance (5) bank documentation (6) no protected-class language (7) no recent retaliation timing.
legal_standard_detailed: SF Tenant Right to Counsel + BayLegal + Housing Rights Committee counsel test 8-point checklist (see lawyer_review_checklist.csv). Free counsel will challenge any missing element.
application_to_unit1_vs_unit2: Maintain folder per unit: license copy anniversary calc notice copy mailing certificate bank ledger no threats.

question: Can landlord offer discount to one unit not the other without discrimination?
short_answer: Yes if discount is neutral (e.g. hardship accommodation under reasonable accommodation / COVID hardship) but must be documented as accommodation not preference.
legal_standard_detailed: Fair Housing reasonable accommodation (disability) may require rent flexibility; SF hardship under §37.7 petitions may relieve passthrough — different discounts lawful if neutral/ accommodation basis.
application_to_unit1_vs_unit2: Document accommodation request + interactive process; do not label as favoritism.

question: Is there case for raising neither unit this year?
short_answer: Yes — zero increase always lawful and preserves goodwill; bank preserved for later so no legal loss; normal for relationship-driven small landlord.
legal_standard_detailed: Zero increase does not forfeit bank; bank adds to future; many small landlords skip low CPI years (0.7–1.4%) as not worth friction.
application_to_unit1_vs_unit2: If friction cost high skip year document bank; revisit after 2027 figure published Mar 2027.
practical_recommendation: Zero is reasonable normal business practice — especially 1.6% small.
